annotations.description: Vodalian Arcanist is about to die in combat to Midnight Guard (1/3 vs 2/3). The player has Acrobatic Maneuver available at exactly 3 mana with the opponent fully tapped out. Casting it would save the Arcanist, draw a card, and trigger Distinguished Conjurer for 1 life — all pure upside. Instead, the player passes and lets the Arcanist die for nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Vodalian Arcanist to die in combat.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Vodalian Arcanist to save it from combat death, draw a card, and trigger Distinguished Conjurer for 1 life. The opponent is tapped out so there's no reason to hold the mana.

annotations.description: Valley attacked Vodalian Arcanist into Midnight Guard, presumably planning to save it with Acrobatic Maneuver, but then declined to cast the trick. The Arcanist dies in combat for nothing. Casting Acrobatic Maneuver would have saved the creature, drawn a card, triggered Distinguished Conjurer for 1 life, and the whole line was clearly the reason for the attack in the first place.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting Vodalian Arcanist die to Midnight Guard in combat.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Vodalian Arcanist (had exactly {W}{W}{U} available for the {2}{W} cost) to save the creature, draw a card, and trigger Distinguished Conjurer.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Acrobatic Maneuver with 3 untapped mana and no other castable spells this turn. The spell would have drawn a card (cantrip value) and flickered Distinguished Conjurer for minimal but non-zero value. Instead, 3 mana goes completely unused.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, declining to cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Distinguished Conjurer
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Distinguished Conjurer to draw a card and make use of available mana, since no other 3-mana or less plays were available this turn.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Acrobatic Maneuver when they had exactly 3 mana available and no other castable spells this turn. Casting it on Vodalian Arcanist (tapped) would draw a card, untap the Arcanist, and gain 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer's trigger. The cantrip could help find land drops to cast the expensive cards in hand (Teferi, Preston, Chimera all cost 4+). However, saving Acrobatic Maneuver for later synergy with Preston (creating token copies of flickered creatures) is a reasonable consideration.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting Acrobatic Maneuver, wasting 3 available mana with no other plays possible this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Vodalian Arcanist to cantrip (drawing toward land drops for the expensive hand), untap the Arcanist, and gain 1 life. The card draw is especially valuable when the hand is full of 4-5 mana spells and they need lands.

annotations.description: Valley could have blocked Midnight Guard with Distinguished Conjurer and cast Acrobatic Maneuver to exile/return the Conjurer before damage. This would prevent 2 damage, draw a card, gain 1 life from Conjurer's ETB trigger, and keep the Conjurer alive. With exactly 3 untapped lands and no other instant-speed plays affordable, there was no meaningful opportunity cost.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not block, taking 2 damage from Midnight Guard
annotations.betterLine: Block Midnight Guard with Distinguished Conjurer, then cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Conjurer before damage. This prevents 2 damage, draws a card, gains 1 life, and preserves the Conjurer.

annotations.description: Casting Knightly Valor (a 5-mana aura) taps out completely into an opponent with 7 cards in hand and blue mana available. The opponent already had Leave in the Dust in their graveyard, suggesting they play bounce spells. If the enchanted creature gets bounced, it's a devastating 2-for-1. Additionally, the opponent could have Exclude if targeting a creature spell, though Knightly Valor isn't a creature spell.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Knightly Valor for 5 mana, tapping out completely
annotations.betterLine: A safer line would be Gideon's Lawkeeper (1 mana) + Forced Worship on a blocker (2 mana) = 3 mana, leaving 2 mana open for Valorous Stance as protection. Or Lawkeeper + Dub on Skyhunter Patrol (4 mana total, leaving 1 open), which still makes a 4/5 flying first striker while keeping the aura investment smaller and deploying an additional creature.

annotations.description: Player chose Flicker of Fate ({1}{W}) over Acrobatic Maneuver ({2}{W}) to blink Distinguished Conjurer at end of turn. With exactly 3 untapped lands and no other use for the mana, Acrobatic Maneuver would have provided the same blink effect plus drawn a card. The extra mana would have gone to waste anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Flicker of Fate to blink Distinguished Conjurer, gaining 1 life but no card draw.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Distinguished Conjurer to get the same blink/life gain plus draw a card, since all 3 mana was available and unused at end of turn.

annotations.description: Cast Exclude (counter target creature spell + draw) during their own postcombat main with no creature spell on the stack. Exclude requires a creature spell as a target - casting it here accomplishes nothing and wastes a valuable counterspell. Even if the game somehow allows it to resolve drawing a card, it's far better held for the opponent's turn to counter their next creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Exclude with no valid target on the stack, wasting a counterspell
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority to hold up Exclude for the opponent's turn to counter their next creature spell. If wanting to use 3 mana, Acrobatic Maneuver on Distinguished Conjurer would draw a card and gain 1 life from the ETB trigger while keeping the counterspell for later.

annotations.description: Cast Magnanimous Magistrate (6 mana, slow value engine) while Teferi, Master of Time sits at 4 loyalty threatening to take over the game. The opponent was fully tapped out, making this an ideal window to kill Teferi.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Magnanimous Magistrate for 6 mana, using all available mana and not addressing Teferi.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dub on Skyhunter Patrol (3 mana) to make it a 4/5 flying first striker, then attack Teferi to kill it (4 damage vs 4 loyalty). Could also cast Gideon's Lawkeeper (1 mana) and hold 2 mana for Valorous Stance to protect against removal. Killing Teferi before it accumulates value is critical.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Teferi's +1 loyalty ability (draw a card, discard a card) during postcombat main phase. This is free card selection that also increases Teferi's loyalty from 4 to 5, making it harder for the opponent's Skyhunter Patrol to kill Teferi. Teferi can be activated once per turn, and skipping this turn's activation wastes an opportunity for card filtering with a 6-card hand that includes situational cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Teferi, Master of Time's +1 ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Teferi's +1 to loot (draw then discard), getting card selection and bringing Teferi to 5 loyalty for better survivability against the opponent's flyers.

annotations.description: Attacking Teferi at 5 loyalty with 4 total power won't kill it (reduces to 1), and the opponent can -3 to phase out an attacker before damage, leaving Teferi at 3. Meanwhile, attacking the player at 12 life applies meaningful pressure. Either way Teferi likely uses -3, but going face deals real damage while Teferi's loyalty drops from its own usage.
annotations.actionTaken: Directed all attackers at Teferi, Master of Time
annotations.betterLine: Attack the opponent directly to deal 2-4 damage to their 12 life total, since Teferi will likely -3 defensively regardless and won't die from 4 damage anyway

annotations.description: Chose Gallant Cavalry over Settle Beyond Reality when the Magnanimous Magistrate (3/4 with 5 reprieve counters) is an extremely dangerous threat that can recursively return creatures like Archon of Justice from the graveyard. Settle Beyond Reality could exile the Magistrate AND flicker Distinguished Conjurer for additional value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Gallant Cavalry (3W) to create two 2/2 vigilance bodies.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Settle Beyond Reality (4W) using 2 Plains + 2 Islands + Vodalian Arcanist's mana, choosing both modes to exile Magnanimous Magistrate and flicker Distinguished Conjurer for life gain. Removing the Magistrate prevents recursive value from Archon of Justice and other creatures in the graveyard.

annotations.description: Discarded Teferi's Ageless Insight when Teferi, Master of Time is on the battlefield at 3 loyalty. The Insight would turn every Teferi +1 activation into 'draw 2, discard 1' - an incredibly powerful card advantage engine. The hand had weaker options to discard like Thraben Inspector (a 1/2 with a clue token).
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Teferi's Ageless Insight
annotations.betterLine: Discard Thraben Inspector instead. Teferi's Ageless Insight has extraordinary synergy with the active Teferi on board and would generate overwhelming card advantage if resolved. Thraben Inspector is the lowest-impact card in hand.

annotations.description: Midnight Guard (2/3) attacks Teferi at 3 loyalty, dealing only 2 damage and leaving it at 1. The Skyhunter Patrol (4/5 with Dub, flying, first strike) can one-shot Teferi by itself since 4 > 3 loyalty. Sending the Midnight Guard at the player would deal 2 damage to their 14 life total while Skyhunter handles Teferi alone.
annotations.actionTaken: Directed Midnight Guard's attack at Teferi, Master of Time (3 loyalty), dealing 2 of the needed 3 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack the player with Midnight Guard (2 damage face) and send Skyhunter Patrol at Teferi to kill it in one hit (4 damage > 3 loyalty), getting maximum value from both attackers.

annotations.description: Double-blocked Midnight Guard (2/3) instead of Magnanimous Magistrate (3/4). Blocking Magistrate with both 2/2s would kill the much more dangerous creature (3/4 with 5 reprieve counters that can recur creatures) while only losing one token, and would take 1 less damage (6 total vs 7). Midnight Guard is far less threatening than a Magistrate that can recur the opponent's creatures when they die.
annotations.actionTaken: Double-blocked Midnight Guard with Gallant Cavalry and Knight Token, letting Magnanimous Magistrate deal 3 damage unblocked.
annotations.betterLine: Double-block Magnanimous Magistrate with Gallant Cavalry and Knight Token to kill it (4 damage vs 4 toughness), losing one 2/2 to its 3 power but eliminating the much more dangerous threat and taking 1 less damage.

annotations.description: Casting Valorous Stance during combat when all opponent's lands are tapped and the only threat is Teferi's -3 (phasing out), which indestructible doesn't prevent. There are no opponent creatures with toughness 4+ to destroy either. The card is likely wasted for no meaningful effect.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Valorous Stance during combat
annotations.betterLine: Hold Valorous Stance for a later turn when it could destroy a high-toughness creature or protect against actual destroy effects. Pass priority here since the opponent's lands are all tapped and can't respond with anything except Teferi's phase-out, which indestructible doesn't stop.

annotations.description: Casting Thraben Inspector in precombat main untaps the opponent's Midnight Guard (which triggers 'whenever another creature enters, untap this creature'). This gives the opponent a 2/3 blocker that was previously tapped, potentially preventing the Knight Token 2/2 from attacking profitably.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thraben Inspector before combat, untapping opponent's Midnight Guard
annotations.betterLine: Attack first with Knight Token 2/2 (and possibly other creatures) while Midnight Guard is tapped, then cast Thraben Inspector and other spells in the postcombat main phase.

annotations.description: Settle Beyond Reality allows choosing one or both modes at no additional cost. The player only chose mode 1 (exile opponent's creature) when they could have also chosen mode 2 (flicker own creature). Flickering Thraben Inspector would create a free Clue token and trigger Distinguished Conjurer for 1 life gain — pure upside for zero additional mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected only mode 1 (exile target creature you don't control) for Settle Beyond Reality
annotations.betterLine: Select both modes — exile an opponent's creature AND flicker Thraben Inspector to get a free Clue token plus Distinguished Conjurer life trigger

annotations.description: Used Gideon's Lawkeeper to tap Vodalian Arcanist, which was already tapped. This completely wastes the Lawkeeper's tap ability for the turn, accomplishing nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted the already-tapped Vodalian Arcanist with Gideon's Lawkeeper's tap ability.
annotations.betterLine: Target Distinguished Conjurer, which is untapped and has a powerful activated ability that enables ETB value loops. Tapping it prevents both blocking and its blink ability.

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main with 3 untapped mana and two Clue tokens available to crack (2 mana each) plus Acrobatic Maneuver castable. Drawing cards is important when behind on board, and this mana will go to waste. At minimum, cracking a Clue token for a card draw is pure upside here since there are no instant-speed plays worth holding up 2 mana for (opponent's threats are mostly tapped).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using any mana, wasting the opportunity to draw a card.
annotations.betterLine: Crack a Clue token for 2 mana to draw a card, preserving Acrobatic Maneuver for potential defensive use. Alternatively, cast Acrobatic Maneuver on Vodalian Arcanist to draw a card and gain 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer's trigger.

annotations.description: With opponent's Preston, the Vanisher on the stack, casting Acrobatic Maneuver now (before Preston resolves) would avoid the downside of Preston creating Illusion token copies of Valley's creatures whenever they're flickered later. After Preston resolves, every blink effect Valley uses will give the opponent a free token copy. Additionally, Acrobatic Maneuver is a cantrip that draws a card and triggers Distinguished Conjurer for 1 life - pure value that's better used now than later.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Preston to resolve without responding
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Distinguished Conjurer in response to Preston on the stack, drawing a card and gaining 1 life from Conjurer's ETB trigger, without giving the opponent an Illusion token from Preston

annotations.description: Used Gideon's Lawkeeper to tap a summoning-sick 2/2 Drake Token instead of Preston, the Vanisher (2/5). Preston is a much more effective blocker due to its 5 toughness - it can wall Midnight Guard (2/3) and trade favorably with Magnanimous Magistrate (3/4). Tapping Preston would open up much better attacks.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped a 2/2 Drake Token with Gideon's Lawkeeper
annotations.betterLine: Tap Preston, the Vanisher (2/5) to remove the biggest blocker and enable more profitable attacks with Midnight Guard and Magnanimous Magistrate

annotations.description: Forced Worship was put on the Drake Token 2/2 flyer instead of Preston, the Vanisher 2/5. Preston is the more dangerous card overall - it's a larger body (2/5 vs 2/2) and enables a powerful value engine with Distinguished Conjurer's flicker ability. While Forced Worship doesn't stop Preston's triggered/activated abilities, preventing 2 more damage per attack and forcing the opponent to spend 2W to bounce it seems more impactful than neutralizing a single 2/2 Drake.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Forced Worship on Drake Token 2/2
annotations.betterLine: Put Forced Worship on Preston, the Vanisher 2/5 to neutralize the larger body and force the opponent to invest mana to free it

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with multiple available actions including Opt (pure cantrip), Acrobatic Maneuver (which with Preston in play would create an Illusion token copy + draw a card), and Clue Token activations. All of these generate card advantage at no meaningful cost.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with unspent mana and unused card advantage opportunities.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Distinguished Conjurer to get a Preston Illusion token copy, gain 1 life, and draw a card. If mana remains, also cast Opt or crack a Clue. At absolute minimum, cast Opt for free card selection.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Drake Token (2/2 flying) when all opponent's creatures were tapped, missing 2 free damage. Opponent goes to 13 instead of 11.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Vodalian Arcanist, Distinguished Conjurer, and Preston (4 total damage), leaving Drake Token back.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures including the Drake Token for 6 total damage, since the opponent has no untapped blockers.

annotations.description: By passing priority with Opt in hand while the Clue Token ability is on the stack, GPT54 Valley missed the opportunity to cast Opt in response. Casting Opt first would allow a scry 1 before the Clue draw resolves, giving better card selection by potentially bottoming an unwanted card before drawing from the Clue.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting the Clue Token draw resolve without casting Opt in response.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Opt in response to the Clue Token ability on the stack. Scry 1 (potentially bottom a bad card), draw from Opt, then draw from the Clue with improved card quality.

annotations.description: With the Clue Token's draw ability on the stack, casting Opt in response would allow the scry 1 to filter before both the Opt draw and the Clue draw. By passing and letting the Clue resolve first, the scry from Opt only filters before one draw instead of two, losing a small amount of card selection value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting the Clue ability resolve without responding with Opt.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Opt in response to the Clue ability on the stack. Scry 1 (put unwanted card on bottom), draw from Opt, then draw from Clue - maximizing the value of the scry by filtering before both draws.

annotations.description: Faith's Fetters on Preston, the Vanisher does not stop Preston's triggered ability (creating token copies when nontoken creatures enter without being cast). It only prevents the activated 'sacrifice 5 Illusions' ability and attacking/blocking. Preston's main threat is the triggered ability, which continues to function. Meanwhile, the Drake Token 2/2 with flying is the opponent's primary damage source and is unaddressed.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Preston, the Vanisher with Faith's Fetters
annotations.betterLine: Target the Drake Token 2/2 with flying with Faith's Fetters to stop the opponent's main aerial clock and gain 4 life, going from 13 to 17. The Drake is the immediate threat dealing 2 flying damage per turn.

annotations.description: Tapped Vodalian Arcanist (a 1/3 mana producer) with Gideon's Lawkeeper instead of the Drake Token 2/2 with flying. The Drake is the only creature that can attack and deal unblockable flying damage this turn. The Arcanist only provides 1 colorless mana for instants/sorceries, and the opponent's lands are mostly tapped anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Vodalian Arcanist with Gideon's Lawkeeper
annotations.betterLine: Tap the Drake Token 2/2 to prevent 2 unblockable flying damage this turn

annotations.description: Not chump-blocking with the 0/1 Illusion token to save 2 damage. The 0/1 Distinguished Conjurer Illusion token has very little practical value (unlikely to accumulate 5 Illusions for Preston's ability), while 2 life points could matter in a race.
annotations.actionTaken: Took 2 damage from Midnight Guard by declining to block.
annotations.betterLine: Block Midnight Guard with the 0/1 Distinguished Conjurer Illusion token to prevent 2 damage at minimal cost.

annotations.description: With 0 cards in hand and 4 untapped mana that will go unused, the player declined to bounce Forced Worship back to hand. This wastes mana that could have been used to get a reusable removal spell, especially since Faith's Fetters may already be covering a key threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on activating Forced Worship's bounce ability, leaving 4 mana unused with an empty hand.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Forced Worship to return it to hand for 2W, giving a replayable removal spell for future turns instead of wasting the mana.

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main with 7 untapped lands and a Clue Token available to crack for 2 mana. Drawing a card is pure upside here, especially at 12 life with only Sage's Row Savant and Island in hand. Could also have activated Distinguished Conjurer to flicker a creature with Preston on board, generating an Illusion token and life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using any activated abilities.
annotations.betterLine: Crack the Clue Token for 2 mana to draw a card, then consider activating Distinguished Conjurer (5 mana remaining) to flicker a creature and generate a Preston Illusion token copy plus 1 life from Conjurer's ETB trigger.

annotations.description: Put Teferi's Protege on top instead of Inspiring Overseer during Scry 2. Inspiring Overseer is a 2/1 flyer that draws a card and gains life on ETB - pure card advantage that synergizes extremely well with Preston, the Vanisher and Distinguished Conjurer already on board. Teferi's Protege only offers looting (draw + discard), which is strictly worse card selection without card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Teferi's Protege on top of library, sending Inspiring Overseer to the bottom.
annotations.betterLine: Put Inspiring Overseer on top. It provides card advantage (draw without discard), evasive flying damage, life gain, and excellent synergy with Preston (blink creates token copies that also draw cards) and Distinguished Conjurer.

annotations.description: Used Gideon's Lawkeeper to tap Sage's Row Savant, which is summoning sick and already unable to attack or use tap abilities this turn. This wastes the Lawkeeper's tap ability for the turn cycle.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Sage's Row Savant (summoning sick, can't attack anyway) with Gideon's Lawkeeper
annotations.betterLine: Tap the Drake Token 2/2 (flying) to prevent it from attacking, since it's the only untapped creature that can meaningfully attack this turn and flies over the player's ground blockers.

annotations.description: With 0 cards in hand and 9 untapped lands (all opponent lands tapped), the player could have bounced Forced Worship back to hand for {2}{W}, then potentially redeployed it on the most threatening creature (like Preston 2/5 or the Drake Token) this same turn for {1}{W}, total 5 mana with 9 available. This would allow redirecting the lock to the best target while having flexibility. Instead, they passed with no other plays available.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without bouncing Forced Worship, leaving all 9 untapped lands unused with an empty hand.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Forced Worship's bounce ability for {2}{W} to get it back in hand, then replay it on the most threatening untapped creature (likely Preston, the Vanisher 2/5 or Drake Token 2/2) during the postcombat main phase.

annotations.description: GPT54 Valley declined to block the attacking Midnight Guard (2/3) despite having Preston, the Vanisher (2/5) available as a free blocker. Preston would survive the combat easily (taking only 2 damage, remaining as 2/5 with 2 damage) and prevent 2 damage to Valley's life total. There is no downside to this block.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to block, taking 2 damage to go from 18 to 16 life.
annotations.betterLine: Block Midnight Guard with Preston, the Vanisher. Preston survives at 2 damage marked (2/5 body vs 2 power) and Valley takes no damage. This is a completely free block.
